items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I also saw May Mezzrow, the wife of Mezz Mezzrow. She was a cook in a restaurant in town.

ctx.x: In September, I was engaged for a concert in Antwerp with Ben Webster, Buddy Tate, Jimmy Woody, Wallace Bishop, Milt Buckner and Joe Turner. It was nice to blow with those guys who were all friends.

Then I went to Copenhagen and made a tour with a nice Danish trombone player, John Darville and his group. They were nice musicians and pals and we played Arhus, Holback and did a radio show. Then I went to Oslo, my first time in Norway, and played with a dixieland band, the Big Chief Jazz Band. All were very nice fellows and we had a ball and drank quite a bit. We played at the Dow Tow Key Club and did a T.V. I went back to Denmark. I saw my old friend Timmie Rosenkrantz and his wife Inez Cavanaugh. He had a…

Buddy Tate had been in Paris and in Europe for a concert tour. I asked him if he would be interested to make a record with me for Pathe-Marconi. He liked very much the idea but had difficulties with the manager who had brought him in Europe. Jean-Marie Monnestier who was against the idea. He told Buddy that if he made the record, Monnestier would not pay his fare back to the U.S.A. So until the last minute, we still did not know if he would be there for the recording.
